THE CUNNING CONMAN

By: Nicky Troll | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Locked up, but not shut down: how a master conman is still robbing farmers of their hard earned cash and livestock almost a decade later - all orchestrated from inside prison.

Unique Selling Point:
• An unusual scam with a twist.... the con-artist is sitting behind bars.
• Opportunity to follow up on a story we exposed 9 years ago.
• Exposes the weaknesses within Correctional Services AGAIN, we’ve done similar investigations before – nothing seems to have been done by the authorities to address the issue.

Summary:
Next level criminals not only have access to the outside world - but are running extensive cons from inside. This we know. We’ve done multiple stories. But this time round, the same con is running a very similar scam, still targeting the farming industry STILL from behind bars.

We trace the steps of one his most recent cons, connect the dots and demand answers from the Minister of Correctional Services.


Further information:
BACKGROUND
Times are tough in the farming industry. The economy and the climate has taken it’s toll on many farmers, with more and more farms up for sale.

A conman is exploiting their desperation – pretending to buy farms using stolen details and fake proof of payments only to steal their livestock.

LATEST CASE
Piet du Toit was selling 280 sheep in November, one man contacts to buy them all. Receives POP, the sheep leave on a truck – but two days later still no payment (R700k). Truck driver dropped them off in Welkom / Theunissen. No one knows where they’ve gone or who bought them. 117 sheep left alive.

Petrus Hendrik van Rooyen is the man that did the deal. But was it the real Van Rooyen?

NO, after a team of private investigators traced the transporter’s route, they recovered just over 100 sheep and then the twist – the local authorities know the scam and the scammer. After sharing audio of the man’s voice it’s confirmed by Du Toit’s people that it’s the same man. But he’s not anyone, he’s the same man we exposed in 2017.

THE CONMAN
This is a very successful conman – buying farms and making off with the farmer’s livestock with fake POPs using stolen identities for more than a decade all from behind bars. The Conman is Joseph Nguru – he operates from inside prison – not just in 2017 when we first exposed him - since 2011 right up until 2026.

The Farming community has become the playground of this very inventive conman. He’s knowledgeable and sounds like older, Afrikaans farmer who knows the business and speaks the lingo.

He uses different aliases – usually the name of the previous farmer he scammed because during the sale process he would have gotten all the details – ID’s, contact addresses, etc. So when the new mark does his due diligence – there will be a legitimate person, who is in the farming industry by that name usually with other properties on their name.

Joseph Ngure grew up on farms in the Free State – in 2017 he was serving a sentence in the Kroonstad Prison for fraud and stock theft, his old MO was to physically cut fences and steal live stock. Since then he has been found guilty on the MO we exposed in 2017 – and is now serving his sentence in Grootvlei Prison close to Bloemfontein.

BREAK DOWN OF THE ORIGINAL MO
The Conman responds to For Sale ads for farms and livestock. He makes an offer, signs the offer to purchases with comprehensive details and sends through a proof of payment. Sometimes he’ll send through a foreman to inspect the farm while the deal is going on making it seem legit – this is often an unwitting person thinking he’s found a new job. Then he’ll want to move the livestock and starts making arrangements. Often he’s dealing with farmers in areas that have bad cellphone reception or where the farmers aren’t physically on the land. A livestock transporter will arrive and make off with the livestock – it’s either sold at an auction or to butchery or another farmer. Before you know you know it, the animals are gone and there is no sign of the money in your bank account.

The foreman & transporter are NOT part of the con – they have ALSO been conned! They don’t get payment for their services and are left out of pocket.

THE MO ADAPTED
In recent years he’s adapted the scam when he realised farmers were onto him. From conning estate agents to transporters and farm managers looking for work – the list of victims is long and covers the whole of SA.

He’ll offer employment, he’ll overpay and need a refund, he’ll buy livestock with fake POPs, he’ll sell non-existent livestock – whatever it takes.

He pretended he had overpaid – asks for money paid back, drawn in cash and dropped off with his outside accomplices.

THE CONSTANT
While the MO’s change – he is always using a stolen ID of legit farmer, he speaks perfect Afrikaans with a convincing accent using the right lingo, asking the right questions. The POPs are ALWAYS fake.

THE ELEMENTS OF STORY TELLING
- NEW CASE STUDY – PIET DU TOIT’s 280 sheep
- TRACE THE STEPS WITH PI TO WELKOM
- REVEAL IT’s OUR JOSEPH NGURU
- RECAP HIS ACTIVITY IN RECENT YEARS
- TELL THE STORY OF THE NEW MO WITH A SECOND PI WHERE THE CASH WAS WITHDRAWN HANDED OVER TO ACCOMPLICES IN 2022.
- A LAWYER IN BLOEMFONTEIN ACTUALLY WENT TO THE PRISON TO DEMAND A RAID BE DONE ON HIS CELL WHEN SHE FIGURED OUT HER CLIENT WAS BEING CONNED – multiple simcards were recovered – that was 2022.
- THAT MADE NO DIFFERENCE – HE’s STILL BUSY – WE HAVE VOICE RECORDINGS AND WHATSAPP OF HIS LATEST ATTEMPT TO BUY A FARM FROM FEB 2026.
- CONFRONT CORRECTION SERVICES

INTERVIEWS
• MINISTER OF CORRECTIONAL SERIVCES
• RIAAN DU PLESIS - PIET DU TOIT’s FINANCIAL MANAGER
• DAVE VAN HEERDEN – PRIVATE INVESTIGATOR THAT TRACED THE SHEEP AND CONNECTED TO JOSEPH NGURU
• PETER KLUGE – PRIVATE INVESTIGATOR THAT FIGURED OUT THE FARM MANAGER MIDDLEMEN ANGLE WITH THE CASH PAYMENT AT THE WELKOM CASINO
• LAWYER THAT WENT TO THE PRISON AND CAN TELL THE STORY OF THE RAID, THE SIM CARDS AND THE PHONES THAT WERE RECOVERED.
• PRESENTER ELEMENT – PIECING THE EVIDENCE TOGETHER - BUIDLING A MAP OF THE CASES
• THE FARMERS WILL FEATURE WITH VOICE CLIPS AND THE MAPS

FINAL SCRIPT | THE CUNNING CON

VO: On farms across the country, drought and volatile markets are taking a toll.

AUDIO MOMENT- SHEEP

VO: And when farmers are forced to sell, their desperation can make them targets for con artists.

UPSOUND AUDIO CALLS TO VICTIMS
VOICE 1: Onmiddelik toe kontak die bliksem my, maar hy praat Afrikaans soos ek en jy.
SUB: Immediately, the bastard contacted me, but he speaks Afrikaans just like you and I.
VOICE 2: Hy klink soos ‘n ou oom boer en hy ken van alles.
SUB: He sounds like an old farmer uncle, and he’s knowledgeable about everything.

RIAAN: If the guy talks to you, it's really, it's business as usual.

VO: Riaan du Plessis is the financial manager for one of South Africa’s biggest sheep farms.

After a prolonged drought, they decided to put 280 animals on the market at the end of last year.

Quicker than expected, they got an offer from a farmer in the Eastern Cape, a Mr Van Rooyen.

RIAAN: It was actually a very easy deal. Pricing wasn't questioned. And actually, he phoned more than once to get the, to get the invoice because he wanted to make the payment.

VO: The proof of payment for R644 000 came through on a Thursday afternoon. The sheep were loaded, and the truck set off for Edenburg in the Eastern Cape the next day.

But by the Monday morning, the money still hadn't reflected.

RIAAN: I phoned Mr. Van Rooyen, he said, I'm very sorry, man, me and my wife, we are in the bank now, your money would be in the bank by 4:00 and then added in a sense of, by the way, comment or by the latest tomorrow morning, 9:00. And then I knew that this is a problem.

VO: Riaan appointed a Private Investigator.

PAUSE
Tracking the transporter’s route, Braam Joubert discovered that the truck was diverted by Mr. Van Rooyen to the Free State.

GOVAN: This is where you found the sheep Braam?
BRAAM: Yes, in this kraal here.
GOVAN: You can immediately see this is not someone who can afford to buy 600,000 rands of sheep.
BRAAM: Definitely not.

VO: With 119 sheep recovered, the hunt for the elusive Mr Van Rooyen began. Braam’s first lead was a voice recording.

UPSOUND VOICE NOTE:
SUSPECT FARMER: Ek gaan saam met Neels kom. Ek is gewoond om op ‘n trekker te sit.
SUB: I’ll come with Neels. I’m used to sitting on a tractor.

GOVAN: He sounds like he's. someone is sitting on a farm in the Free State.
BRAAM: Yes, yes, yes. …

VO: We tracked down the apparent buyer: a Mr van Rooyen from the Eastern Cape. At first, it seemed we'd found our man.

UPSOUND CALL RINGING

GOVAN: Ek hoor Meneer is besig om plase te koop en vee reg oor die land – is dit dieselfde Meneer Van Rooyen.
SUB: I hear you’re busy buying up farms and livestock across the country - is this the same Mr van Rooyen?
VAN ROOYEN: Ek is die regte PH Van Rooyen. Iemand het my identiteit gesteel en ja – hulle gebruik dit om plase en vee te koop maar dis nie ek nie.
SUB: No, I am the real PH Van Rooyen. Someone’s stolen my identity and, yes, they’re using it to buy farms and livestock, but it’s not me.

VO: The voice recordings are actually of a man who hasn’t set foot on a farm since at least 2011 .

UPSOUND CLIPS….We’re working with sheep and so on, so do you think we’ll be able to drive out by Wednesday.

VO: And it turned out to be a voice we'd heard before... in a context more correctional than agricultural.

LINK: This is a voice that we know from 2017, and it may sound unbelievable, but this isn't an Afrikaans farmer - it's a criminal, and he's sitting behind bars.

VO: Back then, we exposed a man running precisely the same scam. His name was Joseph Nquru.

DEVICE TO REWIND – TREAT FOOTAGE - UPSOUND 2017
CROOK: Hello, hoe gaan dit daar?
ENGLISH: Hello, how is it going there?
DEVI Where are you at the moment?
CROOK: I’m in Nelspurit, ma’am.
VO: WRONG
DEVI: You’re in Kroonstad Prison right now aren’t you?
CROOK: You must not even do any allegation against me. CUTS CALL

VO: Nine years later, Nquru is still in prison and facing more allegations.

PAUSE

VO: Dr. Pieter Groenewald is the Minister of Correctional Services.

UPSOUND – Mic-ing up and settling

GOVAN: Could you tell me why it persisted even though we exposed him before.
MINISTER : Because I was not the minister since 2017, I only became the minister in July, 23, 2024. Yes, we have a problem, that’s what I inherited.

VO: We’ve spoken to close to twenty people who’ve had contact with Nquru in the past five years. Fourteen of them had combined losses of around R2.5 million .

UPSOUNDS VICTIM CALLS -
CALL 1: We lost about I think R320 000.
CALL 2: It was in the region of about R80 000
CALL 3: Ek het R300 000 by hom verloor. SUB: He took me for R300 000.

VO: We uncovered cases from 2025 and even an attempted con as recently as February this year.

GOVAN: He's continued to scam farmers under your watch - so you haven't been able to stop him, Minister.
MINISTER : I, as Minister, are not informed of each and every contravention taking place all over the 243 prisons. The moment it was brought to my attention, I acted immediately.. He's transferred. He's not even in the Free State anymore.

VO: But Nquru’s location is irrelevant to how he appears to operate.

LINK: Joseph Nquru has been behind bars for at least 15 years. And in that time he cycled through all these prisons. But he was always connected to the outside world.

VO: And that’s possible because of an issue bigger than this case alone: the availability of cell phones. These recent images from three different prisons show the extent of the problem.

GOVAN: As you can see there, these inmates don't only have cell phones, they also have, charges.
MINISTER: Okay. No, no, no…. Let's make a deal.
GOVAN: Yep.
MINISTER : Between me and you, if you get those photos send it to me..

PAUSE BUTTON…

VO: But that’s not how the media’s relationship with sources works. The point is that cell phones are still getting into prisons and the scams are continuing.

It’s alleged that there are at least 40 cases against Joseph Nquru, for crimes committed while he’s been in prison.

LINK: Over the years, he's changed how he conducts the con, and by doing so it's spread across the country. From Van Zyl Rus in the Northern Cape to Donnybrook in KZN, he's changing his tactics.

VO: A scam in Welkom several years ago is an example. Within days of advertising two farms for sale, a client of private investigator Peter Kluge, got a R32 million cash offer and an additional 5 million for all the cattle.

PETER: The purchaser got hold of my client and said, oh by the way, if you look at the figure that I've paid you, I've overpaid you about 220,000 rand. I need to move my cattle from my existing farm to your farm. It's going to cost 184,000 rand. Won't you please just transfer that money into this bank account?
GOVAN: At that point did any money reflect in your client’s account?
PETER: Nothing, that’s when they obviously called me. I traced the bank account owner.

VO: It emerged that, while posing as a wealthy farmer, Nquru had employed a farm manager. That’s who the account belonged to.

PETER: He got this call from this farmer saying, this is a beautifully well spoken Afrikaans farmer. I've got a job for you. You fit the criteria. I'm employing you, here it is. The way he got to his bank account is he said to you need to pay wages. I'm going to put money in your account. There’s 184,000 rand coming and I R184,000 arrived. So the guy thought, well here we go, we’re in business - I've got a job.
GOVAN: Was this farm manager in on the scam?
PETER: No he wasn't, I think he suffered a fair loss as well because he had to travel up to Welkom, to meet people to pay the balance of the cash.
GOVAN: He thought he was paying wages, he was….
PETER: Well he thought he paid the wages.
GOVAN: But in reality...
PETER: He paid, he paid the suspect, in reality.

AUDIO BEAT

GOVAN: South Africans surely deserve to be protected from being scammed by people inside prison?
MINISTER: Of course.
GOVAN: And Minister, it's your job to protect South Africans.
MINISTER: Yes. And I will do it. But it is also the responsibility of the South African Police Services to ensure that they catch the people.

VO: But, in this case, that’s what happened. He’s behind bars.

MINISTER: It is also the responsibility of the Justice Department. NO, no, no, give me a chance… it's also the responsibility of the Justice Department to ensure that there are convictions,

VO: But that's what happened: Nquru is a convicted criminal serving a sentence.

MINISTER : But it is also the responsibility of the public, not and make sure that they do not fall for the scam.
GOVAN: Who should the farmers blame when they've been scammed by someone who's sitting in prison?
MINISTER : Well, firstly, they must ask themselves, why did they fall for this scam, were they can I say very suspicious about the thing?

VO: Let’s listen to the voice clips again.

UPSOUND VOICE NOTE: Wikus vorder daarso? Hoe ver is julle van die eers trop?
SUB: Wikus, how’s it going there? How far are you from the first flock?

VISUALLY BRING IN POP

VO: And then there’s the proof of payment – seems authentic.

PETER: There’s only one word and it’s cunning. It's an ingenious way that he's done this. The problem is you're going to convict him of fraud or theft or whatever it may be, he's going to sit in prison, but he's already in prison.

VO: And that’s no impediment to his scam, even when the authorities are alerted.

In 2022, attorney Chenique Snyman figured out the so-called buyer behind a collapsed R6 million farm sale, was calling her from a maximum-security prison .

CHENIQUE: We made an appointment to see the head of the prison there. To inform him of the ongoing fraudulent activity of one of the inmates.
GOVAN: Did they do anything about it at the prison?
CHENIQUE: They said they did a search of his cell, and they found two hands full of disposable sim cards that he was busy using. They presented the contraband to us that they have found, it was as if they were pleased with themselves for finding it.

VO: Confiscating devices is one thing, stopping the network is another.

GOVAN: The question really is who is running a correctional centres the inmates or the department?
MINISTER : LAUGHS - No…straightforward, I said we will do everything. We have budget constraints, but I prioritize certain moneys to ensure that we get more modern technology.
MINISTER : We started with a pilot project, and there are three facilities, where we have monitoring equipment, modern technology and if a cell phone is used in the facility, we can pick it up immediately.

VO: That’s just 1.2% of prisons. But the minister insists raids and clean-ups are delivering results. 37 000 cellphones confiscated, 180 officials dismissed in one financial year.

GOVAN: 180 people brought in, 37,000 cellphones?
MINISTER: Well, how many do you want me to fire?.
GOVAN: I don't think those numbers match up.
MINISTER : NO, let me now be clear, I don't think you understand correctional services in South Africa.

VO: What we do understand is that correctional services is where convicted criminals go to serve jail time, not to commit more crime.

CHENIQUE: This is the matter where the public is not even safe from inmates, then what is the use of them being locked up?

END
PROMOS


PROMO 1
VO: A relentless conman targeting farmers…

PETER: There’s only one word and it’s cunning. // It's an ingenious way that he's done this

VO: He’s raked in millions…

CALL 1: We lost about I think R320 000.
CALL 3: Ek het R300 000 by hom verloor. SUB: He took me for R300 000.

VO: All orchestrated from behind bars - with stolen identities and fake proof of payments.


PROMO 2
VO: A cunning conman locked up but still at it...

GOVAN: He’s continued to scam farmers under your watch //
MINISTER: I, as Minister, am not informed of each and every contravention…//

VO: So the victims keep paying. We expose an elaborate scam run from inside prison.



PROMO 3
VO: A conman - locked up but not stopped.

PETER: There’s only one word - it’s cunning.

VO: Scamming farmers out of millions.

VOICE 2: Hy klink soos ‘n ou oom boer en hy ken van alles.
SUB: He sounds like an old farmer uncle, and he’s knowledgeable about everything.

VO: We expose an elaborate scam - all orchestrated from inside prison.

Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 22 March 2026 TX Date: 0000-00-00 Script: FINAL SCRIPT | THE CUNNING CON VO: On farms across the country, drought and volatile markets are taking a toll. AUDIO MOMENT- SHEEP VO: And when farmers are forced to sell, their desperation can make them targets for con artists. UPSOUND AUDIO CALLS TO VICTIMS VOICE 1: Onmiddelik toe kontak die bliksem my, maar hy praat Afrikaans soos ek en jy. SUB: Immediately, the bastard contacted me, but he speaks Afrikaans just like you and I. VOICE 2: Hy klink soos ‘n ou oom boer en hy ken van alles. SUB: He sounds like an old farmer uncle, and he’s knowledgeable about everything. RIAAN: If the guy talks to you, it's really, it's business as usual. VO: Riaan du Plessis is the financial manager for one of South Africa’s biggest sheep farms. After a prolonged drought, they decided to put 280 animals on the market at the end of last year. Quicker than expected, they got an offer from a farmer in the Eastern Cape, a Mr Van Rooyen. RIAAN: It was actually a very easy deal. Pricing wasn't questioned. And actually, he phoned more than once to get the, to get the invoice because he wanted to make the payment. VO: The proof of payment for R644 000 came through on a Thursday afternoon. The sheep were loaded, and the truck set off for Edenburg in the Eastern Cape the next day. But by the Monday morning, the money still hadn't reflected. RIAAN: I phoned Mr. Van Rooyen, he said, I'm very sorry, man, me and my wife, we are in the bank now, your money would be in the bank by 4:00 and then added in a sense of, by the way, comment or by the latest tomorrow morning, 9:00. And then I knew that this is a problem. VO: Riaan appointed a Private Investigator. PAUSE Tracking the transporter’s route, Braam Joubert discovered that the truck was diverted by Mr. Van Rooyen to the Free State. GOVAN: This is where you found the sheep Braam? BRAAM: Yes, in this kraal here. GOVAN: You can immediately see this is not someone who can afford to buy 600,000 rands of sheep. BRAAM: Definitely not. VO: With 119 sheep recovered, the hunt for the elusive Mr Van Rooyen began. Braam’s first lead was a voice recording. UPSOUND VOICE NOTE: SUSPECT FARMER: Ek gaan saam met Neels kom. Ek is gewoond om op ‘n trekker te sit. SUB: I’ll come with Neels. I’m used to sitting on a tractor. GOVAN: He sounds like he's. someone is sitting on a farm in the Free State. BRAAM: Yes, yes, yes. … VO: We tracked down the apparent buyer: a Mr van Rooyen from the Eastern Cape. At first, it seemed we'd found our man. UPSOUND CALL RINGING GOVAN: Ek hoor Meneer is besig om plase te koop en vee reg oor die land – is dit dieselfde Meneer Van Rooyen. SUB: I hear you’re busy buying up farms and livestock across the country - is this the same Mr van Rooyen? VAN ROOYEN: Ek is die regte PH Van Rooyen. Iemand het my identiteit gesteel en ja – hulle gebruik dit om plase en vee te koop maar dis nie ek nie. SUB: No, I am the real PH Van Rooyen. Someone’s stolen my identity and, yes, they’re using it to buy farms and livestock, but it’s not me. VO: The voice recordings are actually of a man who hasn’t set foot on a farm since at least 2011 . UPSOUND CLIPS….We’re working with sheep and so on, so do you think we’ll be able to drive out by Wednesday. VO: And it turned out to be a voice we'd heard before... in a context more correctional than agricultural. LINK: This is a voice that we know from 2017, and it may sound unbelievable, but this isn't an Afrikaans farmer - it's a criminal, and he's sitting behind bars. VO: Back then, we exposed a man running precisely the same scam. His name was Joseph Nquru. DEVICE TO REWIND – TREAT FOOTAGE - UPSOUND 2017 CROOK: Hello, hoe gaan dit daar? ENGLISH: Hello, how is it going there? DEVI Where are you at the moment? CROOK: I’m in Nelspurit, ma’am. VO: WRONG DEVI: You’re in Kroonstad Prison right now aren’t you? CROOK: You must not even do any allegation against me. CUTS CALL VO: Nine years later, Nquru is still in prison and facing more allegations. PAUSE VO: Dr. Pieter Groenewald is the Minister of Correctional Services. UPSOUND – Mic-ing up and settling GOVAN: Could you tell me why it persisted even though we exposed him before. MINISTER : Because I was not the minister since 2017, I only became the minister in July, 23, 2024. Yes, we have a problem, that’s what I inherited. VO: We’ve spoken to close to twenty people who’ve had contact with Nquru in the past five years. Fourteen of them had combined losses of around R2.5 million . UPSOUNDS VICTIM CALLS - CALL 1: We lost about I think R320 000. CALL 2: It was in the region of about R80 000 CALL 3: Ek het R300 000 by hom verloor. SUB: He took me for R300 000. VO: We uncovered cases from 2025 and even an attempted con as recently as February this year. GOVAN: He's continued to scam farmers under your watch - so you haven't been able to stop him, Minister. MINISTER : I, as Minister, are not informed of each and every contravention taking place all over the 243 prisons. The moment it was brought to my attention, I acted immediately.. He's transferred. He's not even in the Free State anymore. VO: But Nquru’s location is irrelevant to how he appears to operate. LINK: Joseph Nquru has been behind bars for at least 15 years. And in that time he cycled through all these prisons. But he was always connected to the outside world. VO: And that’s possible because of an issue bigger than this case alone: the availability of cell phones. These recent images from three different prisons show the extent of the problem. GOVAN: As you can see there, these inmates don't only have cell phones, they also have, charges. MINISTER: Okay. No, no, no…. Let's make a deal. GOVAN: Yep. MINISTER : Between me and you, if you get those photos send it to me.. PAUSE BUTTON… VO: But that’s not how the media’s relationship with sources works. The point is that cell phones are still getting into prisons and the scams are continuing. It’s alleged that there are at least 40 cases against Joseph Nquru, for crimes committed while he’s been in prison. LINK: Over the years, he's changed how he conducts the con, and by doing so it's spread across the country. From Van Zyl Rus in the Northern Cape to Donnybrook in KZN, he's changing his tactics. VO: A scam in Welkom several years ago is an example. Within days of advertising two farms for sale, a client of private investigator Peter Kluge, got a R32 million cash offer and an additional 5 million for all the cattle. PETER: The purchaser got hold of my client and said, oh by the way, if you look at the figure that I've paid you, I've overpaid you about 220,000 rand. I need to move my cattle from my existing farm to your farm. It's going to cost 184,000 rand. Won't you please just transfer that money into this bank account? GOVAN: At that point did any money reflect in your client’s account? PETER: Nothing, that’s when they obviously called me. I traced the bank account owner. VO: It emerged that, while posing as a wealthy farmer, Nquru had employed a farm manager. That’s who the account belonged to. PETER: He got this call from this farmer saying, this is a beautifully well spoken Afrikaans farmer. I've got a job for you. You fit the criteria. I'm employing you, here it is. The way he got to his bank account is he said to you need to pay wages. I'm going to put money in your account. There’s 184,000 rand coming and I R184,000 arrived. So the guy thought, well here we go, we’re in business - I've got a job. GOVAN: Was this farm manager in on the scam? PETER: No he wasn't, I think he suffered a fair loss as well because he had to travel up to Welkom, to meet people to pay the balance of the cash. GOVAN: He thought he was paying wages, he was…. PETER: Well he thought he paid the wages. GOVAN: But in reality... PETER: He paid, he paid the suspect, in reality. AUDIO BEAT GOVAN: South Africans surely deserve to be protected from being scammed by people inside prison? MINISTER: Of course. GOVAN: And Minister, it's your job to protect South Africans. MINISTER: Yes. And I will do it. But it is also the responsibility of the South African Police Services to ensure that they catch the people. VO: But, in this case, that’s what happened. He’s behind bars. MINISTER: It is also the responsibility of the Justice Department. NO, no, no, give me a chance… it's also the responsibility of the Justice Department to ensure that there are convictions, VO: But that's what happened: Nquru is a convicted criminal serving a sentence. MINISTER : But it is also the responsibility of the public, not and make sure that they do not fall for the scam. GOVAN: Who should the farmers blame when they've been scammed by someone who's sitting in prison? MINISTER : Well, firstly, they must ask themselves, why did they fall for this scam, were they can I say very suspicious about the thing? VO: Let’s listen to the voice clips again. UPSOUND VOICE NOTE: Wikus vorder daarso? Hoe ver is julle van die eers trop? SUB: Wikus, how’s it going there? How far are you from the first flock? VISUALLY BRING IN POP VO: And then there’s the proof of payment – seems authentic. PETER: There’s only one word and it’s cunning. It's an ingenious way that he's done this. The problem is you're going to convict him of fraud or theft or whatever it may be, he's going to sit in prison, but he's already in prison. VO: And that’s no impediment to his scam, even when the authorities are alerted. In 2022, attorney Chenique Snyman figured out the so-called buyer behind a collapsed R6 million farm sale, was calling her from a maximum-security prison . CHENIQUE: We made an appointment to see the head of the prison there. To inform him of the ongoing fraudulent activity of one of the inmates. GOVAN: Did they do anything about it at the prison? CHENIQUE: They said they did a search of his cell, and they found two hands full of disposable sim cards that he was busy using. They presented the contraband to us that they have found, it was as if they were pleased with themselves for finding it. VO: Confiscating devices is one thing, stopping the network is another. GOVAN: The question really is who is running a correctional centres the inmates or the department? MINISTER : LAUGHS - No…straightforward, I said we will do everything. We have budget constraints, but I prioritize certain moneys to ensure that we get more modern technology. MINISTER : We started with a pilot project, and there are three facilities, where we have monitoring equipment, modern technology and if a cell phone is used in the facility, we can pick it up immediately. VO: That’s just 1.2% of prisons. But the minister insists raids and clean-ups are delivering results. 37 000 cellphones confiscated, 180 officials dismissed in one financial year. GOVAN: 180 people brought in, 37,000 cellphones? MINISTER: Well, how many do you want me to fire?. GOVAN: I don't think those numbers match up. MINISTER : NO, let me now be clear, I don't think you understand correctional services in South Africa. VO: What we do understand is that correctional services is where convicted criminals go to serve jail time, not to commit more crime. CHENIQUE: This is the matter where the public is not even safe from inmates, then what is the use of them being locked up? END PROMOS PROMO 1 VO: A relentless conman targeting farmers… PETER: There’s only one word and it’s cunning. // It's an ingenious way that he's done this VO: He’s raked in millions… CALL 1: We lost about I think R320 000. CALL 3: Ek het R300 000 by hom verloor. SUB: He took me for R300 000. VO: All orchestrated from behind bars - with stolen identities and fake proof of payments. PROMO 2 VO: A cunning conman locked up but still at it... GOVAN: He’s continued to scam farmers under your watch // MINISTER: I, as Minister, am not informed of each and every contravention…// VO: So the victims keep paying. We expose an elaborate scam run from inside prison. PROMO 3 VO: A conman - locked up but not stopped. PETER: There’s only one word - it’s cunning. VO: Scamming farmers out of millions. VOICE 2: Hy klink soos ‘n ou oom boer en hy ken van alles. SUB: He sounds like an old farmer uncle, and he’s knowledgeable about everything. VO: We expose an elaborate scam - all orchestrated from inside prison.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Locked up, but not shut down: how a master conman is still robbing farmers of their hard earned cash and livestock almost a decade later - all orchestrated from inside prison.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: • An unusual scam with a twist.... the con-artist is sitting behind bars. • Opportunity to follow up on a story we exposed 9 years ago. • Exposes the weaknesses within Correctional Services AGAIN, we’ve done similar investigations before – nothing seems to have been done by the authorities to address the issue.
metadata.Summary: Next level criminals not only have access to the outside world - but are running extensive cons from inside. This we know. We’ve done multiple stories. But this time round, the same con is running a very similar scam, still targeting the farming industry STILL from behind bars. We trace the steps of one his most recent cons, connect the dots and demand answers from the Minister of Correctional Services.
metadata.Further information: BACKGROUND Times are tough in the farming industry. The economy and the climate has taken it’s toll on many farmers, with more and more farms up for sale. A conman is exploiting their desperation – pretending to buy farms using stolen details and fake proof of payments only to steal their livestock. LATEST CASE Piet du Toit was selling 280 sheep in November, one man contacts to buy them all. Receives POP, the sheep leave on a truck – but two days later still no payment (R700k). Truck driver dropped them off in Welkom / Theunissen. No one knows where they’ve gone or who bought them. 117 sheep left alive. Petrus Hendrik van Rooyen is the man that did the deal. But was it the real Van Rooyen? NO, after a team of private investigators traced the transporter’s route, they recovered just over 100 sheep and then the twist – the local authorities know the scam and the scammer. After sharing audio of the man’s voice it’s confirmed by Du Toit’s people that it’s the same man. But he’s not anyone, he’s the same man we exposed in 2017. THE CONMAN This is a very successful conman – buying farms and making off with the farmer’s livestock with fake POPs using stolen identities for more than a decade all from behind bars. The Conman is Joseph Nguru – he operates from inside prison – not just in 2017 when we first exposed him - since 2011 right up until 2026. The Farming community has become the playground of this very inventive conman. He’s knowledgeable and sounds like older, Afrikaans farmer who knows the business and speaks the lingo. He uses different aliases – usually the name of the previous farmer he scammed because during the sale process he would have gotten all the details – ID’s, contact addresses, etc. So when the new mark does his due diligence – there will be a legitimate person, who is in the farming industry by that name usually with other properties on their name. Joseph Ngure grew up on farms in the Free State – in 2017 he was serving a sentence in the Kroonstad Prison for fraud and stock theft, his old MO was to physically cut fences and steal live stock. Since then he has been found guilty on the MO we exposed in 2017 – and is now serving his sentence in Grootvlei Prison close to Bloemfontein. BREAK DOWN OF THE ORIGINAL MO The Conman responds to For Sale ads for farms and livestock. He makes an offer, signs the offer to purchases with comprehensive details and sends through a proof of payment. Sometimes he’ll send through a foreman to inspect the farm while the deal is going on making it seem legit – this is often an unwitting person thinking he’s found a new job. Then he’ll want to move the livestock and starts making arrangements. Often he’s dealing with farmers in areas that have bad cellphone reception or where the farmers aren’t physically on the land. A livestock transporter will arrive and make off with the livestock – it’s either sold at an auction or to butchery or another farmer. Before you know you know it, the animals are gone and there is no sign of the money in your bank account. The foreman & transporter are NOT part of the con – they have ALSO been conned! They don’t get payment for their services and are left out of pocket. THE MO ADAPTED In recent years he’s adapted the scam when he realised farmers were onto him. From conning estate agents to transporters and farm managers looking for work – the list of victims is long and covers the whole of SA. He’ll offer employment, he’ll overpay and need a refund, he’ll buy livestock with fake POPs, he’ll sell non-existent livestock – whatever it takes. He pretended he had overpaid – asks for money paid back, drawn in cash and dropped off with his outside accomplices. THE CONSTANT While the MO’s change – he is always using a stolen ID of legit farmer, he speaks perfect Afrikaans with a convincing accent using the right lingo, asking the right questions. The POPs are ALWAYS fake.
